editorial:
Ever wonder why some movies fail at the box office but become legends years later? You get a front-row seat to that mystery here. Instead of a scripted story, you get to hang out with real-life legends like Russ Meyer and Cameron Mitchell. They sit down and chat about the weird, wild, and wonderful world of B-movies and oddball cinema. The vibe is like sitting in a cozy lounge with a group of old movie pros who have seen it all and aren't afraid to tell the truth about how the sausage gets made.

What really works is how honest these people are about their careers. You will love hearing the behind-the-scenes stories that never made it into the official press releases. The pacing is steady, though it feels more like a long conversation than a fast movie. If you love movie trivia, you should definitely track this down. Since it is an older piece, you might want to grab the Blu-ray for your physical collection to get the best quality, or see if you can find a digital rental on Apple TV for a quick watch.
endingExplained: Since this is a documentary, there is no big plot twist or fake-out. Instead, the film wraps up by bringing all the different interviews together to define what a cult film actually is. The final scenes show that these movies survive because they have a heart and a style that big studios are too scared to try. It ends with a feeling of respect for the outsiders who kept weird cinema alive.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves movie history and weird B-movies.
